chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu al-Subah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
He said regarding the Words of the Mighty and Majestic: 'And those who do not witness Al-Zur' — He said: 'Al-Ghina' (singing/music).

key_terms.الزُّور: Falsehood; what is false or vain
key_terms.عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: The Mighty and the Majestic (honorific for God)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic term 'Al-Zur' refer to according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) interprets the Quranic term 'Al-Zur' (falsehood or vanity) in Surah Al-Furqan as specifically referring to 'Al-Ghina' (singing/music), thereby grounding the jurisprudential ruling on music in divine revelation. This interpretation is significant in Shia fiqh as it links the spiritual corruption of 'falsehood' directly to the aesthetic and auditory realm of music, often cited alongside the concept of 'Lahw' (diversion) to argue for its prohibition or caution.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, from Abu Al Sabbah,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said regarding the Words of the Mighty and Majestic [25:72] And they who are not witnessing (attending) what is false. Heasws said: ‘The singing (music)’.
en.sarwar: 6. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim from abu al-Sabbah al-Kinaniy who has said the following:

“About the meaning of the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘. . . those who do not attend al-Zur,’ [25:72] abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘It (al-Zur’ah) is music (and singing).”’
